then: A slave in a minister's house in Egypt. Doors locked, the wife pressing him. He chose the door and got caught at it anyway. {trap}She spoke first, as the victim.{/trap}
now: You did the right thing and it still blew up. The person who pushed you now tells the manager, the family, the group chat, that {trap}you were the problem.{/trap} {idea}Truth was on him while the lie was being told.{/idea}
old: Doing right protects me from being accused.
new: Doing right leaves evidence. The shirt was torn from the back.
try: Caught in a false version of events? State what happened once, plainly. Then let the torn shirt speak.

title: It was she who sought me. Then a witness spoke.
subtitle: Speaking the truth plainly when accused
then: Accused at the door, Yusuf {idea}did not stand idle but declared the truth.{/idea} Then a witness from her household proposed a test: look at where the shirt was torn. Scholars differed on whether the witness was a grown man or a baby in the cradle.
now: You are blamed in the office for a mistake that was not yours. Silence feels safer, shouting feels fair. {idea}Yusuf said one plain, true sentence{/idea} and let the evidence do the rest.
old: If I am falsely accused, either stay quiet or fight hard.
new: I can calmly say what happened and trust the truth to show itself.
try: If you are blamed unfairly this week, write one calm, factual sentence before replying.

title: Torn from the back means he was running away.
subtitle: Evidence that speaks for the innocent
then: The witness reasoned: if he was fleeing and she pulled him back, {idea}the shirt would tear from behind.{/idea} The same object the brothers once used for a lie, a shirt, {reward}now spoke for his innocence.{/reward}
now: Your word against someone with more power: the manager, the older relative, the popular kid. It feels hopeless. {idea}Truth leaves traces{/idea} — a timestamp, a message, a small detail — and Allah can bring them to light.
old: When it is my word against a powerful person, the truth does not matter.
new: Truth leaves its marks, and Allah can make them speak for me.
try: Keep a short, honest record of any situation where you feel unfairly treated.

title: A torn shirt told the truth when words could not.
subtitle: How the evidence cleared Yusuf
then: The wife of the 'Aziz accused Yusuf at the door. A witness from her own household said: look at how the shirt is torn. Ibn Kathir explains that when her husband saw it {idea}torn from the back{/idea}, he was certain Yusuf had run and she had pursued. He said: {trap}this is a plot of you women.{/trap}
now: Someone tells the manager a story about you before you even walk in. The group chat has already decided. You feel you have to shout to be heard. {idea}Sometimes the quiet facts speak better than you can.{/idea} Truth often leaves a mark.
old: Whoever tells the story first gets believed.
new: Allah can bring the truth out through the smallest detail, even a torn shirt.
try: Next time you are falsely blamed, state the facts once, calmly, and leave the rest to Allah.

title: Keep it quiet, he said, and ask forgiveness.
subtitle: The husband covers the scandal instead of fixing it
then: The 'Aziz now knew the truth. Ibn Kathir says he told Yusuf to {trap}keep silent about what happened{/trap} and told his wife to ask forgiveness for her sin. He was an easy-going man, and he excused her. The family name was protected, but Yusuf was still in the house with the woman who had lied about him.
now: A relative crosses a line at a family gathering. Everyone agrees: let's not talk about it. The one who was wronged is told to just move on. {idea}Silence can protect a reputation and still leave a person unprotected.{/idea}
old: If we keep it quiet, the problem goes away.
new: Covering a wrong is not the same as making it right for the one who was hurt.
try: Think of one situation you hushed up. Ask yourself if someone is still paying for it.

title: The city's women judged her, and gossip spread fast.
subtitle: When a private sin becomes public talk
then: The 'Aziz had asked for silence, but the story spread through the city. Women of the chiefs and princes criticized his wife. Ibn Kathir quotes Muhammad bin Ishaq: {trap}they had heard of Yusuf's beauty and said these words to get a look at him.{/trap} The verse calls their talk scheming, not concern.
now: The voice note forwarded with a sigh: so sad, can you believe it? The comments under someone's bad moment. {trap}Gossip often dresses up as disapproval.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you really want when you pass it on.{/idea}
old: I am only saying what everyone already knows.
new: Talking about someone's fall can be its own hidden appetite.
try: The next piece of gossip that reaches you today, let it stop with you.

title: One look, and the critics cut their own hands.
subtitle: The banquet that silenced the gossips
then: Hearing their talk, the 'Aziz's wife invited them, gave each {trap}a knife and fruit to cut{/trap}, and called Yusuf out. Ibn Kathir says they were so stunned they cut their hands without noticing. They cried: {idea}Perfect is Allah, this is no human, only a noble angel.{/idea} He was given, as an authentic hadith says, half of all beauty.
now: You judge a friend for being swept away by something: a job offer, a person, a habit. Then you meet the same pull and lose your footing in a minute. {idea}It is easy to be firm about a test you have not faced.{/idea}
old: I would never fall for that.
new: The ones quickest to blame were overwhelmed the moment they faced the same thing.
try: Think of someone you judged harshly. Make one quiet dua for them instead.

title: She admitted he refused, then threatened him with prison.
subtitle: A confession and a threat in one breath

row.title: now you see
sub: this is the one you blamed me for

then: In front of the women, the 'Aziz's wife confessed: {idea}I sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused.{/idea} Some scholars said she was telling them about his inner beauty too, chaste inside and out. Then she threatened him openly: {trap}if he does not obey, he will be imprisoned and humiliated.{/trap}
now: Your boss hints that your contract depends on signing off on something wrong. A friend group says you are out unless you join in. {trap}Pressure often comes with a price tag attached to saying no.{/trap} {idea}The no itself is the proof of who you are.{/idea}
old: If refusing costs me this much, maybe I should give in.
new: A threat for refusing is a sign the refusal was right.
try: Name one pressure you are under right now and write down what saying no would protect.

title: Prison is dearer to me than what they call me to.
subtitle: Yusuf chooses the cell and asks for help

row.title: do not leave me to myself

then: Yusuf was young, and the one calling him had beauty, wealth and rank. Ibn Kathir says he {reward}preferred prison{/reward} because he feared Allah. His prayer meant: {idea}if You leave me to rely on myself, I have no power over myself.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ named among the seven shaded on the Day a man invited by such a woman who says, I fear Allah.
now: The late-night message you know you should not answer. The shortcut at work everyone takes. You think: I can handle it. {idea}Yusuf did not trust his strength. He asked Allah not to leave him alone with it.{/idea}
old: I can resist this on my own if I try hard enough.
new: Even the strongest say: Lord, if You leave me to myself, I will fall.
try: Before a moment you know tempts you, say Yusuf's words: Lord, turn it away from me.

title: He asked, and his Lord answered and turned it away.
subtitle: A prayer for protection, heard at once
then: Right after Yusuf's prayer, the verse says {reward}his Lord responded{/reward} and turned their plot away from him. Ibn Kathir says Allah protected him from error and saved him from giving in. The verse ends with two names: {idea}the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.{/idea}
now: You whispered a prayer in the car park before a hard meeting. You asked for help with a habit at 2 a.m. and it felt like nobody heard. {idea}The One who answered Yusuf hears that whisper and knows exactly what you are up against.{/idea}
old: My small private prayers probably do not reach anywhere.
new: A prayer for protection is heard, and the answer can come straight away.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to protect you from one specific weakness.

title: They knew he was innocent and jailed him anyway.
subtitle: Prison to save face
then: Even after they saw {idea}the proofs of his innocence{/idea}, they decided to imprison Yusuf. Ibn Kathir suggests they wanted people to think {trap}Yusuf was the guilty one{/trap}, since the news had spread. Years later he would refuse to leave prison until his name was cleared.
now: The intern blamed so the senior manager keeps his bonus. The child punished because the adult is embarrassed. {trap}Sometimes people know the truth and still choose their image.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees the full file.{/idea}
old: If I am treated unfairly, it must mean my truth did not count.
new: People can bury the truth for a time, but they cannot erase it.
try: If you have let someone else carry blame that was yours, take one step to set it right.

title: Even in prison, people saw goodness in him.
subtitle: Two cellmates bring their dreams to Yusuf
then: Two young men entered the prison with Yusuf. Qatadah said one was {idea}the king's wine-server{/idea} and the other his baker. Each had a dream. They came to Yusuf because, they said, {reward}we see you are one of those who do good.{/reward}
now: You are stuck in a job you did not choose, a hospital ward, a hard season. You think it is wasted time. {idea}People still notice how you treat them there.{/idea} The way you behave in a low place can open the next door.
old: In a place like this, how I act does not matter.
new: Good character shows most clearly in the worst rooms, and people see it.
try: Wherever you feel stuck today, do one kind thing for someone stuck with you.

title: Before the dreams, he told them who taught him.
subtitle: Yusuf uses their trust to point to Allah

row.title: left a way
sub: that denies Allah and the Hereafter

then: Yusuf told the two men he would explain their dreams {idea}before their next food arrived{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he first made clear that {reward}this knowledge was from Allah{/reward}, given because he left the way of people who did not believe in Allah or the Last Day. He called them to Tawhid before interpreting.
now: Someone praises your work in the meeting. Your exam result. The client who says you are a genius. {idea}You can take the compliment and still name where the skill came from.{/idea} Yusuf turned attention from himself to his Lord.
old: My talent is mine, I earned it.
new: Every skill I have was taught to me by my Lord.
try: When someone praises you today, quietly say alhamdulillah and mean it.

title: I follow my fathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub.
subtitle: Belief in One God as a favor, not a burden

row.title: a favor
sub: on us and on all people

then: Yusuf told his cellmates he followed the way of {idea}Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub{/idea} and would never set up partners with Allah. Ibn Kathir explains that this belief is {reward}a grace from Allah to us and to mankind{/reward}, sent through the Messengers. Yet most people do not thank Him for it, as in 14:28.
now: Your grandmother's prayer mat. The way your father said bismillah before driving. You may think of faith as something handed to you, heavy. {reward}It is the best inheritance you were given.{/reward}
old: Religion is a list of things I have to carry.
new: Knowing Allah is a gift passed down to me, and most people forget to thank Him for it.
try: Thank Allah today, by name, for one person who taught you about Him.

title: Many scattered masters, or the One who prevails?
subtitle: A simple question asked in a prison cell
then: Yusuf kept calling his two prison companions. Their people worshipped idols. He asked them plainly: {trap}are many separate lords better{/trap}, or {idea}Allah, the One, the Irresistible{/idea}? Ibn Kathir says everything has submitted to His kingdom.
now: Your boss's approval. Your followers' likes. Your in-laws' opinion. Your bank balance. {trap}Each one is a small master with its own demands.{/trap} {idea}One Lord means one set of expectations to live for.{/idea}
old: I have to keep everyone happy at once.
new: Serving One Master is freedom from serving many.
try: Name one opinion you are living for. Today, do one thing purely for Allah instead.

title: Only names you and your fathers made up.
subtitle: Inherited habits with no proof behind them
then: Yusuf told the men their idols were {trap}only names forged and handed from one generation to the next{/trap}, with no proof from Allah. Ibn Kathir says he affirmed that {idea}judgement and command belong to Allah alone{/idea}, and that this is the straight religion, though most people do not know. Then he turned to their dreams.
now: The family custom nobody questions. The thing everyone at work does because it has always been done. {trap}Habit is not the same as proof.{/trap} {idea}Ask where a rule came from before you give your life to it.{/idea}
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: A tradition needs a source from Allah, not just a long history.
try: Pick one habit you follow without thinking and ask honestly: who said this?

title: Two dreams, two endings, told with care.
subtitle: Yusuf delivers good news and hard news gently

row.title: one of you
sub: softened for the one who grieves

then: Yusuf told them: one of you will pour wine for his master, the other will be crucified. Ibn Kathir notes he {idea}did not address either man directly{/idea}, so the second would grieve less. When they claimed they had seen nothing, he said {trap}the matter is decided.{/trap}
now: The doctor who has to give bad news in the corridor. The manager telling a team about layoffs. You have to tell a friend something they will not want to hear. {idea}Truth does not have to be delivered like a blow.{/idea}
old: Honesty means saying it straight, however it lands.
new: I can tell the whole truth and still choose words that spare the heart.
try: Before you share difficult news with someone today, take one breath and soften the first sentence.

title: Mention me to your master, he asked, but he forgot.
subtitle: A small request, forgotten for years
then: Yusuf knew which man would go free and asked him: {idea}mention me to your king.{/idea} But the man {trap}forgot, a plot of Shaytan{/trap}, and Yusuf stayed in prison for several more years. Mujahid and Qatadah said the word used means between three and nine years.
now: You sent the CV and the contact promised to pass it on. You asked a cousin to put in a word. Months pass. Nothing. {idea}People forget. Allah does not.{/idea} Your name is still on His list.
old: If the person I counted on forgets me, I am stuck.
new: People forget, but the delay can be leading to a better door.
try: Think of a favor someone promised and forgot. Forgive it quietly and make dua for the outcome.

title: The king dreamed, and his whole court was lost.
subtitle: Seven fat cows, seven lean ones
then: The king of Egypt saw a dream that left him {trap}astonished and afraid{/trap}. He gathered priests, chiefs and princes and asked them to explain it. Ibn Kathir says Allah made this dream {idea}the reason for Yusuf's release{/idea}, with his honor preserved.
now: A problem lands on the desk of the most powerful person in the building, and nobody can solve it. You, in the back office, might have the answer. {idea}Allah can turn someone else's worry into your opening.{/idea}
old: The powerful people have nothing to do with my little situation.
new: Allah can move a king's sleep to open a prisoner's door.
try: Write down one closed door in your life and leave it with Allah in dua tonight.

title: Mixed-up dreams, the experts said, and we do not know.
subtitle: The court brushes off what it cannot explain
then: The king's advisers had no answer. Ibn Kathir says that {trap}as an excuse{/trap}, they called it a jumble of false dreams. They added that they were not skilled in interpreting dreams. {idea}Their failure set the stage{/idea} for the man who knew Yusuf to remember.
now: In the meeting, someone asks a question no one can answer, so the room decides it was a silly question. You do it too, with a hard question from your child. {idea}I do not know is a better answer than it does not matter.{/idea}
old: If I cannot explain it, it probably means nothing.
new: Not knowing is honest, dismissing the question to hide it is not.
try: The next time you do not know an answer today, simply say I do not know.

title: After years, the forgetful man finally remembered.
subtitle: The right memory at the right moment

row.title: the freed man
sub: I can tell you, send me

row.title: too late
sub: he should have spoken years ago

then: The man who had left prison {trap}forgot Yusuf for years{/trap}. Now, hearing the court fail, he remembered. Ibn Kathir says he told the king and his circle: {idea}I will tell you its meaning, so send me{/idea} to Yusuf, the man of truth.
now: You applied years ago and heard nothing. Then one day the call comes, exactly when the company is desperate. {reward}The memory came back when it would count most.{/reward} {idea}Delays are not always denials.{/idea}
old: If it did not happen when I wanted, it was never going to.
new: Allah brings the forgotten thing back to mind at the moment it matters most.
try: Message one person you forgot to follow up with. Today might be their right moment.

title: He called him the man of truth.
subtitle: Yusuf's reputation survived the prison walls
then: The freed man went to the prison and greeted Yusuf as {reward}the man of truth{/reward}. He repeated the king's dream word for word so he could {idea}return to the people and they might know.{/idea} The man who had forgotten Yusuf still remembered his character.
now: Years after you left a job, a former colleague still says: ask them, they are honest. {reward}That is the reputation that outlives the CV.{/reward} The title people give you when you are not in the room.
old: Being stuck somewhere low erases who I am.
new: A truthful character keeps its name, even inside a prison.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you said it, even if no one checks.

title: Sow for seven years, store it, and eat a little.
subtitle: Yusuf turns a dream into a plan
then: Yusuf explained the dream {idea}without blaming the man for forgetting him{/idea} and without asking for release first. Ibn Kathir says the cows were years. He advised them to {reward}store the harvest in its ears{/reward} to keep it healthy, eat only what they needed, and avoid extravagance.
now: Payday. The bonus. The good month at the shop. {trap}It is tempting to spend it all because times are good.{/trap} {idea}Yusuf's advice: enjoy a little, save the rest in a way that lasts.{/idea}
old: When things are good, I can relax and spend.
new: The good years are the time to prepare for the hard ones.
try: Put aside one small amount today, money, food, or time, for a harder day.

title: Then seven hard years will eat what you saved.
subtitle: The lean cows explained

row.title: the store saved them
sub: that is what it was for

then: Yusuf told them {trap}seven years of drought{/trap} would follow, the lean cows eating the fat ones. Ibn Kathir says nothing planted then would grow. They would live on {reward}what they had stored{/reward}, except a little they kept back.
now: The emergency fund that goes in one month when the car breaks and the boiler fails. It feels like it vanished. {reward}It did exactly its job.{/reward} {idea}Saving is not lost when a hard season uses it up.{/idea}
old: If my savings get used up, it was all for nothing.
new: What I stored in good times is what carries me through hard ones.
try: Thank Allah for one past hard season that something you prepared got you through.

title: After the drought, a year of rain and pressing.
subtitle: Good news the dream did not even show
then: Yusuf added something the king had not asked about. Ibn Kathir says he gave them {reward}good news{/reward}: after the years of drought would come a year of {idea}abundant rain{/idea}, when the land would produce again and people would press oil and grapes as usual.
now: The year of chemo. The long unemployment. The season of grief. {trap}It feels like it will never lift.{/trap} {reward}Yusuf's answer ends with rain.{/reward} Hard years are counted, not endless.
old: This hard season is just how life is now.
new: Hardship has a number, and after it comes rain.
try: Tell someone going through a hard time one hopeful thing you truly believe.

title: Freedom was offered, and he said: first clear my name.
subtitle: Yusuf refuses to leave until the truth is known
then: The king wanted Yusuf brought to him. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf {idea}refused to leave until his innocence was declared{/idea}, so all would know the prison was an injustice. The Prophet ﷺ praised his patience, saying that if he had stayed in prison as long, {reward}he would have accepted the offer{/reward}.
now: You were let go after a false complaint. Now they want you back, quietly, no questions asked. {idea}Sometimes the right move is to ask for the record to be corrected first.{/idea} Your name matters, not just your exit.
old: When a door opens, grab it before it closes.
new: Leaving with my name cleared can be worth more than leaving early.
try: If there is a misunderstanding about you, ask calmly for it to be cleared, without anger.

title: Now the truth is out: it was I who tried.
subtitle: The confession, years later

row.title: the women
sub: we know no evil of him

then: The king gathered the women who cut their hands and asked what happened. They said: {idea}Allah forbid, we know no evil against him.{/idea} Then the 'Aziz's wife said: {reward}now the truth is plain.{/reward} It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is truthful.
now: Years after the falling out, the person who spread the story finally admits it was not true. Or you are the one who should admit it. {idea}The truth has a way of coming out, and saying it yourself is a mercy.{/idea}
old: Too much time has passed for the truth to matter now.
new: It is never too late for the truth to come out, even from my own mouth.
try: If you once told a story that hurt someone unfairly, correct it with one person this week.

title: Allah does not let the betrayers' plan succeed.
subtitle: The confession and why it was made
then: Ibn Kathir's stronger view is that the 'Aziz's wife continued: I admit this {idea}so my husband knows I did not betray him in his absence{/idea}, and nothing happened. Others said Yusuf said these words. Either way, the verse sets a rule: {trap}Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers.{/trap}
now: The colleague who undermines you in emails you never see. The secret you are keeping from your spouse. {trap}Plots built on betrayal seem to work for a while.{/trap} {idea}They never get where they wanted to go.{/idea}
old: If no one finds out, it does not matter.
new: Betrayal behind someone's back has no path to real success.
try: Do one thing today you would be fine with the other person seeing.

title: I do not claim my self is innocent.
subtitle: The soul pulls toward wrong, unless Allah has mercy
then: In Ibn Kathir's stronger view, the 'Aziz's wife said: {idea}I do not free myself from blame.{/idea} The soul wishes and desires, and that is what drove her. She ended with hope: {reward}my Lord is Forgiving, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: You snapped at your kids, then blamed the traffic. You scrolled what you should not, then blamed the algorithm. {idea}Owning it is the first step back.{/idea} And the One you return to is Forgiving.
old: I only did it because of the situation I was in.
new: My own self pulls me toward wrong, and only Allah's mercy keeps me.
try: Tonight, name one mistake from today without an excuse, and ask Allah to forgive it.

title: From the cell to the king's inner circle.
subtitle: One conversation, and trust was won
then: Once Yusuf's innocence was clear, the king wanted him {idea}as one of his closest aides{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says that when they spoke, the king saw his ability, good conduct and manners, and told him: {reward}today you are with us, high in rank and fully trusted.{/reward}
now: The interview where you just told the truth, did not oversell, did not badmouth your old boss. The new manager says: I trust you. {idea}Years of quiet integrity can show up in a single conversation.{/idea}
old: Getting ahead depends on knowing the right people.
new: Character, kept in hard years, is what opens the door when it finally opens.
try: In one conversation today, just be plainly honest, with no spin.

title: Put me over the storehouses: I guard, and I know.
subtitle: Yusuf asks for the job he is suited for
then: Yusuf asked the king to put him in charge of the land's storehouses. Ibn Kathir says {idea}praising yourself is allowed when your ability is unknown and there is a need{/idea}. He described himself as an honest guard with knowledge of the work, so he could {reward}distribute the harvest wisely{/reward} in the drought.
now: The team needs someone to run the budget, and you know you can do it well. You stay quiet because speaking up feels like bragging. {idea}Saying I can do this, honestly, so people are served, is not arrogance.{/idea}
old: Mentioning my own strengths is always showing off.
new: Offering my real skills when people need them can be a way of serving.
try: Offer one skill you have to someone who needs it this week.

title: No good-doer's reward is ever lost.
subtitle: The slave and prisoner now moves freely in the land
then: Allah says He {reward}established Yusuf in the land{/reward}. Ibn Jarir said he now moved freely after prison, hardship and slavery. Ibn Kathir says Allah did not let {idea}his patience with his brothers and in prison{/idea} be lost, but rewarded it with help and victory.
now: The years you cared for a sick parent. The job where you stayed honest while others cut corners. The marriage you kept kind through hard seasons. {idea}None of it is lost.{/idea} {reward}Allah keeps the record.{/reward}
old: My patience went unnoticed, so it was for nothing.
new: Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
try: Remember one hard thing you were patient through, and thank Allah that He saw it.

title: Power in Egypt, but the Hereafter's reward is better.
subtitle: The bigger prize after the worldly one
then: Right after Yusuf's rise, Allah adds: {reward}the reward of the Hereafter is better{/reward} for those who believe and are mindful of Him. Ibn Kathir says what Allah prepared for Yusuf there is {idea}greater and more honored than the authority he had here{/idea}.
now: The promotion comes. The house is bought. The degree is framed. For a week you feel you have arrived. {idea}This verse says: good, and there is more.{/idea} The best part is not on this side.
old: Worldly success is the final proof that I made it.
new: Even the best success here is smaller than what Allah keeps for the mindful.
try: After your next small win, add one deed meant only for the Hereafter.

title: His brothers stood before him and did not know him.
subtitle: The drought brings them to Yusuf's court
then: The drought spread to Canaan, and Ya'qub sent his sons to Egypt for food. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf was {reward}a mercy to the people{/reward}, giving each family one camel-load. He knew his brothers at once. {trap}They never imagined the boy they sold would become a minister.{/trap}
now: Years later, the person who mocked you at school walks into your clinic, your shop, your office, needing help. They do not recognize you. {idea}How you treat them now is your test, not theirs.{/idea}
old: If I ever meet the people who hurt me, I will make them feel it.
new: When the tables turn, I get to choose to be a mercy.
try: Think of someone who once wronged you. Decide now how you would want to treat them.

title: Full measure, good hosting, and one request.
subtitle: Yusuf asks them to bring his brother

row.title: fair and generous
sub: even to those who hurt him

then: Yusuf {reward}honored his brothers and gave them all they needed{/reward}. As-Suddi reported that they had told him of a brother kept at home. Yusuf asked them to bring him, to show they had told the truth, and reminded them: {idea}I give full measure and I am the best of hosts.{/idea}
now: Your ex-colleague who took credit for your work now needs a reference. You could undersell them. {idea}Yusuf gave full measure to people who once sold him.{/idea} Fairness does not depend on whether they deserve it.
old: People who wronged me do not deserve my full fairness.
new: Full measure is my standard, whoever is standing in front of me.
try: Give someone you dislike exactly what is fair to them today, no less.

title: No brother next time, then no grain.
subtitle: A firm condition to bring the family together
then: After the kindness came a firm line. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf told them: if you come next time {trap}without your brother, you will get no grain{/trap} from me, nor come near me. He was {idea}encouraging them to return{/idea}, and to return with Binyamin.
now: A parent tells a teenager: you can have the car, but only if you are home by ten. A friend sets a boundary that keeps the relationship alive. {idea}Firmness can be a form of love with a purpose.{/idea}
old: Being kind means never setting conditions.
new: A firm condition can serve a good goal, even a reunion.
try: Set one clear, kind boundary today, and say why it matters.

title: We will work on our father, they promised.
subtitle: The same brothers, asking for a son again
then: The brothers promised Yusuf {idea}we will try our best with our father{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they wanted to prove they were truthful. But this was the father they had already {trap}asked once before for a son, and lost him{/trap}.
now: You promise your partner you will be home on time, again. You ask your parents for trust after you broke it last year. {idea}A promise lands on top of your history.{/idea} Rebuilding trust is slow work.
old: If I promise firmly enough, people should believe me.
new: My past actions decide how much my next promise weighs.
try: Keep one small promise today to someone whose trust you once let down.

title: He hid their payment back in their bags.
subtitle: A quiet gift to make them return
then: Yusuf told his servants to put the brothers' goods {reward}back into their saddlebags{/reward} without them knowing. Ibn Kathir notes it was said he did this because {idea}he feared they would have nothing left to trade{/idea} next time, so they could still come back.
now: You slip the money back into your mum's purse after she paid for dinner. You pay a struggling friend's bill without telling them. {reward}Quiet generosity that keeps the door open.{/reward}
old: If I help, they should know it was me.
new: The best help sometimes works best unseen.
try: Do one kind thing today that the person will never trace back to you.

title: Send our brother, we will guard him, they said again.
subtitle: The words Ya'qub had heard once before

row.title: years ago
sub: send Yusuf, we will guard him

row.title: today
sub: send Binyamin, we will guard him

then: Back home, the brothers told Ya'qub {trap}the grain is denied unless Binyamin comes{/trap}, and promised: we will guard him. Ibn Kathir points out these are {idea}the very words they used about Yusuf{/idea}: send him with us tomorrow, we will take care of him (12:12).
now: I'll drive carefully this time. I won't share your secret again. I'll pay you back by Friday. {trap}The exact words you said last time.{/trap} {idea}Same words need different actions to mean something.{/idea}
old: Saying it again with feeling should be enough.
new: When I repeat an old promise, only changed actions make it new.
try: Pick one promise you keep repeating. Do one concrete thing toward it today.

title: Allah is the best guardian, the Most Merciful.
subtitle: Ya'qub moves his trust from his sons to his Lord
then: Ya'qub asked: {trap}shall I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother?{/trap} Then he turned to Allah. Ibn Kathir says he meant: Allah is the most merciful to me, in my old age and my longing, and {reward}I ask Him to return my son to me.{/reward}
now: Your child gets in the car with friends for the first time. Your teenager flies abroad. You cannot control the road. {idea}You can say: Allah is the best guardian, and mean it.{/idea}
old: I have to control everything to keep the people I love safe.
new: I do what I can, and leave the guarding to the One who guards best.
try: Next time someone you love leaves the house, say: Allah is the best guardian.

title: Our money came back, what more could we want?
subtitle: The returned goods become their argument
then: Opening their bags, the brothers found {reward}their goods returned{/reward}. Qatadah said they asked: what more can we want? Ibn Kathir says they used it {idea}to make their case more appealing{/idea}: food for the family, and an extra camel-load if Binyamin came.
now: A refund lands in your account. A colleague covers your shift. You immediately calculate what it means for you. {idea}Pause and ask who was kind, and why.{/idea}
old: Unexpected good just means a better deal for me.
new: Unexpected good is often someone's quiet care, and it is worth noticing.
try: Next time something unexpected and good comes your way, find out who to thank.

title: Swear by Allah, then I will send him.
subtitle: A father's oath and a father's trust
then: Ya'qub said he would not send Binyamin {idea}until they swore by Allah{/idea} to bring him back, unless they were all overwhelmed. When they swore, he said: {reward}Allah is Witness over what we say.{/reward} Ibn Ishaq said he had no choice, since they needed food to survive.
now: You sign the contract. You make the family agreement in the group chat. You shake on the deal. {idea}Remember who is also listening.{/idea} Allah witnesses every promise, yours included.
old: A promise is just between me and the other person.
new: Every promise I make is made in front of Allah.
try: Before you agree to something today, quietly remember that Allah is witness.

title: Enter by different gates, and trust in Allah.
subtitle: Taking precautions while knowing they are not the cause
then: Ya'qub told his sons to {idea}enter Egypt by different gates{/idea}. Ibn 'Abbas and others said he feared the evil eye for them. Yet he added: this cannot help you against Allah. {reward}The decision is only His; in Him I put my trust.{/reward}
now: You lock the door, check the tyres, set the reminder, back up the files. Then the worry still sits on your chest. {idea}Do the sensible thing, then hand the outcome to Allah.{/idea}
old: If I plan well enough, nothing can go wrong.
new: I take my precautions, and the result is still in Allah's hands.
try: After you take a precaution today, say: I put my trust in Allah, and let it go.

title: The gates did not change Allah's decree, but eased a father's heart.
subtitle: What a precaution really does

row.title: precaution controls fate
sub: if I do this, all is safe

then: The sons entered Egypt by different gates as their father said. Allah says it {trap}did not help them at all against His will{/trap}. It was {reward}a need in Ya'qub's heart{/reward} that he fulfilled. Qatadah said he had knowledge and acted on it, but most people do not know.
now: You pack the first-aid kit, read the reviews, text when you arrive. Some of it is really for your own peace of mind. {idea}That is fine. Just do not mistake it for control.{/idea}
old: If something bad happens, my precautions failed.
new: Precautions settle my heart and do my part, the outcome was always Allah's.
try: Notice one worry-habit today and say: I have done my part, the rest is with Allah.

title: I am your brother, do not grieve over what they did.
subtitle: Yusuf reveals himself to Binyamin in private
then: Yusuf honored all the brothers as guests, then {idea}met Binyamin alone{/idea} and told him his story. Ibn Kathir says he told him: {reward}grieve not for what they did to me.{/reward} He asked Binyamin to keep it secret, and planned to keep him in Egypt with honor.
now: Your younger sibling is going through what you went through with the family years ago. You could tell them every bitter detail. {idea}Or you could sit them down and say: I am here, do not be sad.{/idea}
old: When I finally speak, I will tell them how badly I was treated.
new: My first words to someone hurting can be comfort, not my old grievance.
try: Message a sibling or close friend today just to say: I am here for you.

title: The king's bowl hidden in Binyamin's bag.
subtitle: A plan to keep his brother with him
then: After supplying them, Yusuf had {idea}the king's bowl placed in Binyamin's bag{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes it was used for drinking and, in the drought, for measuring grain. Then a crier called out: {trap}O caravan, you are thieves!{/trap}
now: Sometimes a scene looks like a disaster from where you stand: a sudden transfer at work, a delayed flight, an awkward misunderstanding. {idea}You do not see the plan behind it.{/idea} It may be bringing someone together.
old: If it looks like a disaster, it must be one.
new: What looks like trouble from outside can be part of a plan for good.
try: Think of one recent setback and ask: what good might be hidden inside this?

title: What have you lost? they asked, turning back.
subtitle: The brothers face the accusation
then: Hearing the cry, the brothers turned toward the men. Ibn Kathir says they looked at the one calling out and simply asked: {idea}what is it that you have lost?{/idea} {trap}The men who once lied about Yusuf were now the ones accused.{/trap}
now: Security stops you at the shop exit. A colleague says something has gone missing from the office. Your heart races. {idea}Asking a calm question first often helps more than defending yourself loudly.{/idea}
old: When accused, I need to fight back immediately.
new: A calm question can be the strongest first answer to an accusation.
try: The next time someone challenges you, ask one calm question before you defend yourself.

title: The king's measure is missing, and a reward is offered.
subtitle: A camel-load for whoever brings it
then: The men said: {trap}we are missing the king's measuring bowl.{/trap} Whoever brings it gets {reward}a camel-load{/reward} as reward, and the herald added: I guarantee it. Ibn Kathir says this was an assurance that the reward would be delivered.
now: You lose your wallet and offer a reward online. A boss loses a file and offers credit to whoever finds it. {idea}Clear terms and a promise you will honor make people trust you.{/idea}
old: When something is lost, suspicion is the fastest route.
new: A clear offer, backed by a real guarantee, brings things to light more fairly.
try: If you promise someone something today, state it clearly and then keep it.

title: By Allah, you know we are not thieves.
subtitle: The brothers point to their own conduct
then: Accused, the brothers swore: {idea}by Allah, you know we did not come to cause corruption, and we are not thieves.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they meant: since you met us, our good conduct has shown that {reward}theft is not in our character.{/reward}
now: Your manager questions your expenses. You do not need to shout. You can say: you have seen how I work for three years. {idea}A good record speaks before you do.{/idea} So build it on the ordinary days.
old: When accused, only my words can defend me.
new: The way I behave every day becomes my defense on the hard day.
try: Do one ordinary task today so honestly that it would stand up if anyone checked.

title: And if you are lying, what is the penalty?
subtitle: The brothers are asked to set their own terms
then: Yusuf's men did not impose a punishment. They asked the brothers: {idea}what should the thief's penalty be, if you turn out to be liars?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they asked what the punishment would be if the thief was {trap}one of them{/trap}.
now: Your child broke the rule. You ask: what do you think is fair? You are surprised how strict they are with themselves. {idea}The rules we name for others are the rules we will be held to.{/idea}
old: The penalty is for other people, so I can make it harsh.
new: The standard I set for others may be the one I am judged by.
try: Before you judge someone today, ask if you would accept the same verdict yourself.

title: Whoever has it in his bag, he himself is the price.
subtitle: The brothers pronounce their own law
then: The brothers said: {trap}he in whose bag it is found will himself be the penalty.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this was {idea}the law of Ibrahim{/idea}, that the thief is given to the one he stole from. This is exactly what Yusuf wanted.
now: You confidently say: anyone who misses the deadline loses the bonus. Then your own task is the one that is late. {idea}Speak your rules carefully. They have a way of coming back.{/idea}
old: My strict rules are only for people who break them.
new: The law I announce with confidence can be the one that finds me.
try: Rephrase one strict rule you hold for others so you would be fine living by it too.

title: Above every knower is One who knows more.
subtitle: Allah's plan for Yusuf, and the limit of all knowledge
then: Yusuf searched their bags {idea}before his brother's{/idea} to complete the plan. Allah says: thus did We plan for Yusuf. By the king's law he could not take his brother, but {reward}by their own law he could.{/reward} Qatadah said: over every person of knowledge is someone more knowing, until all knowledge ends with Allah.
now: You are the expert in the room, the one everyone asks. Then a new hire explains something you never understood. {idea}There is always someone who knows more, and above everyone, Allah.{/idea}
old: I am the one in this room who knows best.
new: Every bit of knowledge I have sits under someone else's, and all of it under Allah's.
try: Ask someone today to teach you one thing you do not know.

title: He heard the old lie about him and kept silent.
subtitle: Yusuf holds back his reply
then: When the bowl was found, the brothers said: {trap}if he stole, a brother of his stole before{/trap}, meaning Yusuf, to distance themselves. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf {idea}kept his reply to himself{/idea} and did not say it aloud: you are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you describe.
now: In the family group, someone brings up an old, false story about you. You know the truth. You could send the long, angry reply. {idea}Sometimes the strongest answer is the one you keep inside and leave with Allah.{/idea}
old: If someone lies about me, I must correct it immediately.
new: Not every unfair remark needs my answer; Allah knows the truth of it.
try: Next time someone says something unfair, wait before replying, and say inside: Allah knows best.

title: His father is old, take one of us instead.
subtitle: The brothers now plead for their father's heart

row.title: years ago
sub: got rid of the favored son

then: Once Binyamin was to be held, the brothers begged for mercy. Ibn Kathir says they told the 'Aziz: {idea}he has an old father who loves him{/idea}, comforted by him for the son he lost. {reward}Take one of us in his place.{/reward} We see you are a doer of good.
now: The sibling who used to be jealous of you is now the one at the hospital bed, covering your shifts. {idea}People can change.{/idea} The ones who once hurt someone can grow into the ones who protect.
old: People who did wrong once will always be like that.
new: The same people who once caused harm can grow into protectors.
try: Notice one way someone who hurt you in the past has grown, and tell them.

title: Taking the innocent for the guilty would be injustice.
subtitle: Yusuf refuses a swap
then: Yusuf answered: {idea}Allah forbid that we take anyone except the one with whom we found our property.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains, according to the judgement they gave, {trap}taking an innocent man instead would be wrongdoing.{/trap}
now: The whole class gets detention for one pupil. The team loses its bonus for one person's mistake. Someone has to pay, so anyone will do. {idea}Justice cares who.{/idea}
old: As long as someone takes the blame, the matter is settled.
new: Blaming the wrong person is its own injustice, even when it is convenient.
try: If you are tempted to punish a group for one person's fault, address only that person.

title: I will not leave until my father permits me.
subtitle: The eldest brother remembers two broken promises
then: In despair, the brothers {idea}consulted in private{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the eldest, the one who had suggested the well over killing Yusuf, reminded them of {trap}their oath to their father{/trap} and their earlier failure with Yusuf. He said: I will not leave Egypt until my father permits me or Allah decides for me.
now: You promised your parents to look after your younger brother at university, and he has dropped out. You could just go home and shrug. {idea}Or you stay with the problem and take responsibility.{/idea}
old: If it went wrong, I can explain it away and move on.
new: A broken promise calls for owning it, not leaving it behind.
try: Think of one promise you let slip. Take one step this week to make it right.

title: We testify only to what we know.
subtitle: The honest report to their father
then: The eldest told the others to go back and say: {trap}your son has stolen{/trap}, and we testify only to what we know. Qatadah and 'Ikrimah said they meant: {idea}we did not know he would steal{/idea}. We only stated the thief's punishment.
now: Your friend asks what happened between two people at work. You saw part of it. {idea}It is tempting to fill the gaps.{/idea} Saying this is what I saw, and I do not know the rest, is a kind of honesty.
old: When I tell a story, I should give the full picture.
new: I only speak to what I know, and I admit what I cannot see.
try: When you pass on news today, add: this is only what I saw.

title: Ask the town and the caravan, we are telling the truth.
subtitle: When your word alone is not enough
then: The eldest told them to say: {idea}ask the town where we were and the caravan we came with.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they wanted these to confirm their truthfulness and sincere guarding. {trap}After the lie about Yusuf, their own word was no longer enough.{/trap}
now: You tell the truth, and still your parents want to call your friend to check. It stings. {trap}Past lies make honest words need backup.{/trap} {idea}Trust lost takes witnesses to rebuild.{/idea}
old: If I am telling the truth now, people should simply believe me.
new: When I have broken trust before, I may need to show the truth, not just say it.
try: If someone doubts you because of your past, offer them a way to check, without resentment.

title: Beautiful patience, and maybe Allah will bring them all back.
subtitle: Ya'qub's second loss, and a bigger hope

row.title: all together
sub: even the one lost years ago

then: Ya'qub repeated {trap}the same words he said over Yusuf's bloodied shirt{/trap}: your selves have enticed you, so patience is fitting. Then he asked Allah to {reward}bring back all three{/reward}: Yusuf, Binyamin and the eldest who stayed in Egypt. He is the All-Knowing in my distress, the All-Wise.
now: A second miscarriage. Another job loss. A fresh diagnosis on top of an old grief. {idea}Ya'qub's hope did not shrink after the second blow. It grew.{/idea} He asked for everything back.
old: After this second blow, I should stop hoping.
new: The deeper the loss, the bigger my hope in Allah can be.
try: In your dua today, ask Allah for something you had stopped asking for.

title: Oh, my sorrow for Yusuf, and his eyes turned white.
subtitle: A new grief opened the old one
then: Ya'qub turned away from his sons and said: {trap}oh, my sorrow for Yusuf.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the new grief renewed the old one. His eyes went white from crying. Qatadah said he {idea}held in his sorrow and did not complain to any created being{/idea}.
now: Years after your father died, a song in the supermarket and you are in tears again. You feel weak. {idea}A prophet wept until his eyes went white, and he was still patient.{/idea} Grief is not a failure of faith.
old: If I still cry about it, my faith must be weak.
new: Tears and patience can live in the same heart, even a prophet's.
try: Let yourself feel one grief today, then tell it to Allah in a few honest words.

title: You will grieve yourself to death, his sons said.
subtitle: Worry from people who do not understand
then: Ibn Kathir says the sons {idea}felt pity for him{/idea} and spoke out of sorrow: by Allah, you will not stop remembering Yusuf until {trap}your strength leaves you or you die.{/trap} They feared he would die of grief.
now: Your friends say: it has been a year, you need to move on. Your family worries you are stuck. {idea}They mean well.{/idea} But remembering someone you love with hope is not the same as being lost.
old: If I keep remembering them, I am not healing.
new: Others may worry about my grief, but remembering with hope is not giving up.
try: Thank one person who worries about you, and share one thing that gives you hope.

title: I only complain of my grief to Allah.
subtitle: Where Ya'qub took his pain

row.title: to Allah
sub: the One who can fix it

then: Ya'qub answered his sons: {idea}I only complain of my grief and sorrow to Allah{/idea}, and I know from Allah what you do not. Ibn Kathir says he meant: {reward}I expect every kind of good from Allah.{/reward} Ibn 'Abbas said he knew Yusuf's dream was true and would come to pass.
now: The long post about your pain. The fifth friend you have told this week. The vent that leaves you emptier. {idea}Ya'qub took his deepest grief to the only One who could answer it.{/idea}
old: Telling more people will make the pain lighter.
new: Complaining to Allah is not weakness, it is taking the pain to the right address.
try: Tonight, tell Allah about your heaviest worry in your own words, before telling anyone else.

title: Never despair of Allah's mercy.
subtitle: A grieving father sends his sons out to search

row.title: go
sub: search for Yusuf and his brother

then: Ibn Kathir says Ya'qub sent his sons back to {idea}ask about Yusuf and his brother, in a good manner{/idea}. He gave them good news and told them never to give up hope in Allah or stop trusting Him. {trap}Only the disbelieving despair of Allah's mercy.{/trap}
now: The fifteenth rejection email. The test result that did not change. The prayer that seems unanswered for years. {idea}Keep searching. Keep sending the application. Keep praying.{/idea} Despair is the one thing you cannot afford.
old: After this long, it is realistic to give up.
new: Giving up on Allah's mercy is never realistic; I keep acting and hoping.
try: Take one small step today toward something you had stopped hoping for.

title: Hardship has touched us, so be charitable to us.
subtitle: The brothers return, humbled
then: Back in Egypt, the brothers told Yusuf: {trap}hardship has struck us and our family{/trap}, and we have brought little of value. Give us full measure and {reward}be charitable to us{/reward}. Allah rewards the charitable. Ibn Jurayj said they meant: be kind by returning our brother.
now: You walk into the bank, the council office, your estranged sibling's house, needing help. Your pride hurts. {idea}Asking humbly is not a defeat.{/idea} It can be the first step toward healing.
old: Asking for help means I have lost.
new: Coming humbly, with what little I have, can open doors pride kept shut.
try: Ask one person for help you need today, plainly and without excuses.

title: Do you know what you did to Yusuf?
subtitle: The moment Yusuf begins to reveal himself
then: Hearing their hardship and remembering his father's grief, Yusuf felt {idea}compassion and pity{/idea} and wept. Ibn Kathir says he then asked: do you know what you did to Yusuf and his brother, {trap}when you were ignorant{/trap}? When hardship grew hardest, relief came, as Allah says: with hardship comes ease.
now: The moment you finally confront the person who hurt you. You could list every crime. {idea}Or you could say: you did not know what you were doing then.{/idea} The first leaves them defensive. The second leaves room to come back.
old: When I finally confront them, I will make them feel every bit of it.
new: I can name the wrong while leaving the door open for them to return.
try: If you need to raise an old hurt, write the first sentence so it invites, not attacks.

title: I am Yusuf, and this is my brother.
subtitle: Taqwa and patience are never wasted
then: The brothers asked {idea}in amazement: are you really Yusuf?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they had met him for over two years without knowing. He said: I am Yusuf and this is my brother. {reward}Allah has been gracious to us{/reward}, bringing us together. Whoever fears Allah and is patient, Allah does not waste their reward.
now: The moment you finally get the result after years: the visa, the recovery, the reconciliation. Someone asks: how did you do it? {idea}Yusuf's answer: fear Allah, be patient, and He does not waste it.{/idea}
old: I got here because I was smart and worked hard.
new: Taqwa and patience, by Allah's grace, are what got me through.
try: When someone praises your success, tell them one hard moment where you had to be patient.

title: Allah preferred you over us, and we were wrong.
subtitle: The brothers finally admit it

row.title: jealousy
sub: why does father love him more

then: The brothers said: {reward}by Allah, Allah has preferred you over us{/reward}, and we have been sinners. Ibn Kathir says they affirmed his virtue and, above all, his prophethood, and {idea}admitted their error against him{/idea}. The jealousy that began the story ended in an honest confession.
now: The cousin who got the scholarship. The colleague promoted over you. You have quietly resented it for years. {idea}Say it, even just to yourself: Allah gave them this, and I was wrong to resent it.{/idea}
old: Admitting they were preferred means admitting I am less.
new: Accepting what Allah gave someone else, and owning my wrong, sets me free.
try: Say one honest sentence of praise today about someone you have envied.

title: No blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.
subtitle: Forgiveness from the one who had the power to punish
then: Yusuf had the throne, the grain and the power. He said: {idea}no blame on you today.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says he meant: I will not reproach you, and {reward}I will not remind you of it after today.{/reward} Then he went further and prayed for their forgiveness.
now: The family member who finally apologizes for years of hurt. You have the moment to make them squirm. {idea}Or you can say: it is done, I will not bring it up again, may Allah forgive you.{/idea}
old: Forgiving means I still get to remind them now and then.
new: Real forgiveness closes the file and prays for the other person.
try: Pick one old hurt and decide today you will not bring it up again.

title: Take my shirt to my father, and bring the whole family.
subtitle: A shirt brought grief once, now it brings sight
then: Yusuf said: take this shirt and {reward}cast it over my father's face, his sight will return{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says Ya'qub had lost his sight from {trap}excessive crying{/trap}. Then Yusuf asked them to bring all of Ya'qub's children to Egypt.
now: The same hospital where you once lost someone is where your child is born. The house that held hard memories is where the family finally reunites. {idea}Allah can turn the thing that carried grief into the thing that carries joy.{/idea}
old: Some things in my life will always be tied to pain.
new: Allah can make the very thing that brought grief bring healing.
try: Revisit one place or object tied to a hard memory and make a new, good memory there.

title: I smell Yusuf, if you do not call me senile.
subtitle: A father senses the good news before it arrives
then: As the caravan left Egypt, Ya'qub said: {reward}I find the smell of Yusuf{/reward}, if you do not think me senile. Ibn 'Abbas said a wind carried the scent of the shirt to him {idea}from eight days' distance{/idea}. He knew people might laugh at him.
now: You tell your family you feel things are about to turn, the job, the health, the marriage. They roll their eyes. {idea}Hope sometimes senses relief before anyone else can see it.{/idea}
old: If others think my hope is foolish, maybe it is.
new: Real hope can feel relief coming before the evidence arrives.
try: Write down one good thing you are hoping for, and date it.

title: You are still in your old error, they said.
subtitle: A harsh word to a grieving father

row.title: error
sub: love that will not let go

then: Those around him said: {trap}by Allah, you are still in your old error.{/trap} Qatadah said they meant: because of your love for Yusuf, you will never forget him. He added that {idea}this was a harsh word they should never have said{/idea} to their father, nor to a Prophet of Allah.
now: Your elderly mum says something hopeful and the family laughs it off. Dad tells the same story again and you sigh loudly. {idea}A harsh word to a parent stays.{/idea} Choose the gentle one.
old: It is only a small comment, they know I do not mean it.
new: Harsh words to a parent weigh heavily, especially when they are clinging to hope.
try: Call or sit with a parent or elder today and simply listen, without correcting them.

title: The shirt touched his face, and he could see again.
subtitle: Good news arrives, and Ya'qub's hope is proved right
then: Mujahid and As-Suddi said the bearer of good news was Yahudha. As-Suddi added that he had once brought {trap}Yusuf's shirt with false blood{/trap}, so he wanted to erase that error with this good act. The shirt was placed on Ya'qub's face and {reward}his sight came back{/reward}. He said: did I not tell you I know from Allah what you do not?
now: You were the one who broke the bad news, told the lie, caused the rift. Now you can be the one who brings the good news, makes the call, carries the apology. {idea}The hand that did harm can be the hand that heals.{/idea}
old: I caused that hurt, so I am the last person who can fix it.
new: The one who did wrong can choose to carry the good news next.
try: Be the one who delivers a piece of good news or an apology today, in person.

title: Father, ask forgiveness for us, we were wrong.
subtitle: The sons' confession to the one they hurt most
then: Once the truth was out and Ya'qub could see, Ibn Kathir says the brothers came to him {idea}with humbleness{/idea}: {trap}O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; we have been sinners.{/trap} They went to the very person whose heart they had broken.
now: The parent you said hurtful things to as a teenager. The friend you ghosted. Shame makes you want to keep away. {idea}Going back and saying I was wrong, please pray for me, is hard and healing.{/idea}
old: I am too ashamed to face the person I hurt.
new: Going back to the one I wronged and asking for their prayers is the way home.
try: Send one honest message today: I was wrong, please forgive me.

title: I will ask my Lord to forgive you.
subtitle: A father's promise, saved for the right hour

row.title: the best time
sub: the last part of the night

then: Ya'qub said: {idea}I will ask my Lord to forgive you{/idea}; He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Ibn Mas'ud and several others said he {reward}delayed it until the last part of the night{/reward}, to make the prayer at its best time. He forgives those who repent.
now: Your child apologizes. You say: I will pray for you. Then you actually do, at 4 a.m., when the house is quiet. {idea}Praying for someone at the best hour is a gift they never see.{/idea}
old: Saying I will pray for you is just a polite phrase.
new: Promising to pray for someone is a commitment, best kept at the best time.
try: Make a dua tonight before Fajr for someone who has asked you to pray for them.

title: Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety.
subtitle: Yusuf goes out to welcome his parents
then: When Yusuf heard his family was near, Ibn Kathir says he {idea}went out to receive them{/idea}, and the king sent notables with him. He took his parents close and said: {reward}enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety{/reward}, safe from the hardship and famine they had suffered.
now: Your parents arrive at the airport after years apart. You could wait at home. {idea}Go to the gate. Carry the bags. Say: you are safe now.{/idea} Make your welcome match the distance they travelled.
old: I have done well, so they should come to me.
new: Success is a reason to go out and meet my family, not wait for them.
try: Go out of your way today to welcome or visit a parent or elder.

title: This is my dream from long ago, my Lord made it true.
subtitle: Yusuf looks back on the whole road

row.title: you threw me in a well
He took me out of prison

then: His parents and eleven brothers bowed before him, and Yusuf said: {reward}this is my dream from before; my Lord made it true.{/reward} He thanked Allah for taking him out of prison and bringing them from the desert. Notice: {idea}he mentions the prison, not the well{/idea}, and blames Shaytan, not his brothers, for the rift.
now: At the wedding, the graduation, the family dinner after years of tension, you tell the story of how you got here. {idea}You can tell it as a list of who hurt you, or as a list of how Allah helped you.{/idea}
old: Telling my story means naming everyone who wronged me.
new: I can tell my story through Allah's kindness, without reopening old wounds.
try: Write three lines about a hard chapter of your life, mentioning only how Allah helped.

title: At the top of it all, he asked to die a Muslim.
subtitle: Yusuf's prayer when everything was complete
then: With his family reunited and his authority complete, Ibn Kathir says Yusuf asked Allah to {idea}continue His favor into the Hereafter{/idea}: let me die a Muslim and join me with the righteous. The Prophet ﷺ, at his own death, said three times: {reward}O Allah, to the highest companion.{/reward}
now: The best week of your life: the new job, the new baby, the family finally at peace. {idea}That is exactly when Yusuf asked for a good ending.{/idea} Not more of the good times, but to finish well.
old: When life is going well, I just want it to stay this way.
new: At the height of blessing, the wisest prayer is for a good ending.
try: Add Yusuf's words to your prayer today: let me die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.

title: You were not there, yet you know their plot.
subtitle: The story itself is a sign for the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: a lesson and a sign
sub: for him and those who opposed him

then: Some Makkans had asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Israelites in Egypt to test him. Allah revealed the whole story. Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}news of the unseen{/idea}: he was not there when the brothers {trap}plotted to throw Yusuf in the well{/trap}. It carries a lesson for him and a reminder to those who opposed him.
now: You have just finished one of the longest stories in the Quran. You know details no history book in Makkah held. {idea}Pause on that. The story reached you as revelation, not rumor.{/idea}
old: This is just a beautiful old story.
new: This story is a sign of revelation and a lesson aimed at me.
try: Pick one moment from Surah Yusuf that stood out to you and tell someone why.

title: Most people will not believe, however much you want it.
subtitle: Comfort for the one who cares deeply
then: After the proof of the story, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}most people will not believe, even if you eagerly desire it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links this to similar verses, such as: if you follow most of those on earth, they will mislead you. {idea}The numbers are not the measure of truth.{/idea}
now: You share something meaningful with your family, your friends, your colleague. They shrug. You feel you failed. {idea}Your job is to share it with care, not to control their hearts.{/idea}
old: If they do not accept it, I must have failed.
new: Most people may not accept the truth, and that is not on me.
try: Think of someone you keep trying to convince. Make dua for them instead of arguing today.

title: No payment asked, only a reminder for all the worlds.
subtitle: The message is free
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ {idea}asked for no price or compensation{/idea} for his advice and his call to good. He did it seeking Allah's Face and sincere good for people. The Quran is {reward}a reminder to all the worlds{/reward}, so they may be guided and saved.
now: You help a younger colleague, teach your nephew to read Quran, give advice to a friend. {idea}No invoice, no favor to call in later.{/idea} Sincere advice is lighter when nothing is expected back.
old: If I give my time, I should get something for it.
new: The best advice is given freely, for Allah, and for the other person's good.
try: Give one piece of genuinely helpful advice or help today, expecting nothing back.

title: So many signs we walk past without a glance.
subtitle: The heavens and earth, unnoticed
then: Allah says people pass by countless signs in the heavens and earth and {trap}turn away from them{/trap}. Ibn Kathir lists them: {idea}stars and planets, fertile land side by side, mountains, oceans with crashing waves, deserts{/idea}, and fruits alike in shape but different in taste, scent and color.
now: The commute with your head down in your phone. The sunset behind the car park you never look at. The orange you peel without noticing. {idea}Signs, all of them, passed by every day.{/idea}
old: Nature is just the background to my day.
new: The world around me is full of signs I keep walking past.
try: Stop once today, look at one natural thing for a full minute, and say subhanAllah.

title: They believe in Allah, yet set up partners with Him.
subtitle: Faith mixed with something else
then: Ibn 'Abbas said they had part of faith: asked who created the heavens and earth, they said Allah, {trap}yet they worshipped others with Him{/trap}. Al-Hasan applied it to someone who does good deeds {trap}to show off{/trap}. Ibn Kathir also mentions hidden forms, like believing in omens, which the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}Allah removes through trust in Him{/idea}.
now: You pray, then check if anyone saw. You believe in Allah, but a black cat or a broken mirror still ruins your day. {idea}Small things can quietly share the place in your heart that belongs to Allah alone.{/idea}
old: I believe in Allah, so this verse is about other people.
new: Even a believer can let small partners creep in; trust in Allah clears them out.
try: Do one good deed today that no one else will ever know about.

title: Do they feel safe that the Hour will not come suddenly?
subtitle: The danger of feeling too secure
then: Allah asks whether those who set up partners {trap}feel secure from an overwhelming punishment, or the Hour coming suddenly{/trap} while they do not perceive it. Ibn Kathir cites similar verses, which end: {reward}your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: You keep saying: I will sort out my prayer after the exams, after the wedding, after I retire. {idea}None of us is promised that later.{/idea} The good news: the door to Allah is open right now.
old: I have plenty of time to sort myself out later.
new: The Hour comes without notice, so the best time to turn back is now.
try: Do today one thing you have been putting off for later with Allah.

title: This is my way: I call to Allah with clear sight.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ path, and those who follow it
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to declare: {idea}this is my way.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says he called to the testimony that there is no god but Allah {reward}with sure knowledge, certainty and evidence{/reward}, and those who follow him call the same way. Glorified is Allah above any partner.
now: Someone at work asks about your faith. You can bluff, or say: let me find out properly and come back. {idea}Clear sight first, then speaking.{/idea} Following the Prophet ﷺ means learning before teaching.
old: Sharing my faith just means saying something, anything.
new: The Prophet's ﷺ way is calling to Allah with knowledge and clear sight.
try: Learn one thing properly today that someone might ask you about your faith.

title: Travel the earth, and look at how the story ended.
subtitle: Human messengers, and the lessons in ruins
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the messengers were {idea}humans, not angels{/idea}, as some had claimed. Allah asks those who rejected the Prophet ﷺ: have you not travelled and seen {trap}the end of those before you{/trap}? Ibn Kathir says Allah saved the believers, and {reward}the home of the Hereafter is far better{/reward} for them.
now: You visit old ruins on holiday, scroll photos of empty palaces. {idea}Stop and ask: these people were sure of themselves too. What lasted?{/idea} Let the trip become a lesson.
old: Old ruins are just interesting history.
new: The ruins of the past are reminders that only what is with Allah lasts.
try: Next time you see something old and abandoned, pause and think about your own legacy.

title: When hope was nearly gone, Our help came.
subtitle: Victory arrives at the darkest point
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah sends help to His messengers {trap}when distress surrounds them{/trap}. 'A'ishah explained: the trial of the believers was long and help delayed, until the messengers lost hope in their people, and {reward}then Allah's help came{/reward}. Ibn 'Abbas recited: when will Allah's help come? Surely, Allah's help is near.
now: Month eleven of job hunting. The fertility clinic again. The family feud in its fifth year. {trap}It feels like the end of hope.{/trap} {reward}That is the exact point this verse says help arrives.{/reward}
old: If it has not come after all this time, it is not coming.
new: Allah's help often arrives just when hope has run thinnest.
try: Say today, about the thing you have waited longest for: Allah's help is near.

title: In their stories is a lesson for people who think.
subtitle: The close of Surah Yusuf
then: The surah ends by saying the stories of the messengers are {idea}a lesson for people of understanding{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the Quran is not a forged tale but confirms the earlier books and explains what people need. It is {reward}guidance and mercy{/reward}, turning hearts from misguidance to guidance.
now: Jealous brothers. A false accusation. Prison. A family torn apart and brought back together. {idea}Somewhere in Yusuf's story is your own family, your own wait, your own test.{/idea} Find it.
old: Yusuf's story happened long ago to other people.
new: This story is a lesson and a mercy written for my own life.
try: Write down the one lesson from Surah Yusuf you most need right now, and keep it.
